candidates.exact_span: A written submission shall be provided within 5 days of the time the permittee becomes aware of the circumstances.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when a 5-day written noncompliance report was required depends on when the permittee 'becomes aware' and whether the triggering circumstance falls within this reporting category; absent or late submissions affect monitoring/reporting obligation evaluation (B) and whether missing written evidence reflects a waived requirement, documented no-event state, or inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The period of noncompliance including exact dates and times, and if the noncompliance has not been corrected, the anticipated time it is expected to continue
candidates.computation_change_reason: Required report content defines what documented noncompliance periods and ongoing states look like; interpreting available records against these fields changes whether a no-result period is established as documented noncompliance, corrected, ongoing, or unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Any unanticipated bypass which exceeds any effluent limitation in the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'unanticipated bypass,' whether a discharge 'exceeds' an applicable 'effluent limitation,' and which permit limits are implicated determines enforceable limit applicability and exceedance assessment (A), whether 24-hour reporting was required (B), and whether absence of a report reflects a non-triggered condition versus missing evidence of a reportable event (C).

candidates.exact_span: Any upset which exceeds any effluent limitation in the permit
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'upset,' the effluent limitation exceeded, and whether the event is excluded or treated differently under permit terms affects which numeric limits govern compliance comparison (A), 24-hour reporting applicability (B), and classification of undocumented periods around upset events (C).

candidates.exact_span: Violation of a maximum daily discharge limitation for any of the pollutants listed by the Director in Part II (industrial permits only) of the permit to be reported within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This ties 24-hour reporting to Part II maximum daily limits and an 'industrial permits only' qualifier; different readings of whether this permit is industrial, which Part II pollutants are 'listed by the Director,' and what constitutes a maximum daily violation change applicable enforceable limits (A), event-triggered reporting obligations (B), and whether missing 24-hour reports indicate unreported violations or inapplicable requirements (C).

candidates.exact_span: The Director may waive the written report on a case-by-case basis if the oral report has been received within 24 hours.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A waived written report after timely oral reporting is a documented alternative compliance path; without establishing waiver, missing written submissions could be misclassified as inadequate evidence versus an allowed no-written-report state.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall institute a program within 12 months of the effective date of the permit (or continue an existing one) directed towards optimizing the efficiency and extending the useful life of the facility.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability and timing of the Section E pollution-prevention obligation depend on permit effective date and whether an existing program satisfies 'continue an existing one'; different interpretations change which permit-year conditions were actually in force during Federal FY2025.
